_meta.title: GridWise - Extra LLM-Assisted Practice Case Pack
_meta.event: BUP CSE Fest 2026 - Hackathon - Online Preliminary
_meta.description: Ten additional self-authored practice cases built to the same schema and semantics as the public sample pack. Each case carries 1-3 operator notes, the machine-checkable directive interpretation, and one cost-optimal 24-hour reference schedule. These are practice cases only and are not official judge cases.
_meta.generation_note: Each reference schedule was produced by a linear program that minimises total grid cost subject to the interpreted directives, effective solar, battery rate and state-of-charge limits, hourly energy balance and end-of-day battery neutrality, with battery throughput used only as a tie-break among equally cheap plans. Every schedule was then re-validated against those constraints.
how_to_use: Read the official Problem Statement and Participant Guide first; this pack follows their semantics.
POST each case.input object to POST /optimize-energy.
Compare directive_interpretation field by field; free-text explanation wording does not need to match.
Replay the returned hourly_plan against the interpreted directives, effective solar, battery rules, energy balance and end-of-day neutrality.
Equivalent optimal schedules are accepted; total_cost_bdt is the value to match.
Do not hard-code note wording, case IDs, numeric values or reference schedules.

coverage.EXTRA-01: solar_reduction stated as a drop (80% off -> factor 0.2) plus a distractor
coverage.EXTRA-02: minimum_battery_reserve given as an absolute kWh figure
coverage.EXTRA-03: no_discharge_window spanning a single hour, plus a distractor
coverage.EXTRA-05: max_grid_window ending at midnight (hours 22-23, must not wrap)
coverage.EXTRA-06: all notes are distractors; every entry must be no_op
coverage.EXTRA-07: three active directives of three different types in one scenario
coverage.EXTRA-08: percentage-of-capacity reserve overlapping a grid-import cap
coverage.EXTRA-09: no_charge_window and no_discharge_window over identical hours
coverage.EXTRA-10: five-hour hard grid cap that forces pre-charging

interpretation_rules: Return exactly one directive_interpretation entry per operator note, in note_index order.
For no_op: applies must be false and structured_adjustment must be null.
For every non-no_op directive: applies must be true.
Directive hours must be unique integers from 0 through 23 in ascending order.
Time windows are start-inclusive and end-exclusive: 1 PM to 3 PM maps to hours [13, 14].
For solar_reduction, factor is the usable fraction remaining. An 80% reduction means factor = 0.2.
_meta.equivalence_note: The expected_output for each case is one valid optimal reference result. Another schedule is also accepted if it satisfies the same directive ground truth and all GridWise constraints and achieves the same total cost within a 0.01 tolerance.

cases.label: Percentage-drop solar wording plus distractor

operator_notes: A dust storm is forecast from 11 AM to 2 PM and is expected to cut usable rooftop solar output by 80% for that period.
The cafeteria will publish next semester meal plans on Thursday.

directive_interpretation.explanation: An 80% drop leaves 20% of forecast solar usable for hours 11, 12 and 13.
This note carries no schedulable constraint for the 24-hour plan.

expected_output.plan_summary: Treats midday solar as 20% of forecast during the dust storm, ignores the unrelated note, and shifts battery energy into the evening tariff peak while ending at the initial battery level.

cases.rationale: Reduction is stated as a drop rather than a remaining fraction, so factor must be 1 - 0.80 = 0.2. The second note must be no_op.

cases.label: Absolute evening reserve in kWh

operator_notes: Keep at least 90 kWh stored in the battery between 7 PM and 11 PM so the exam halls have backup cover.

directive_interpretation.explanation: A 90 kWh floor applies to stored energy for hours 19 through 22.

expected_output.plan_summary: Holds the 90 kWh evening reserve, buys cheap overnight energy for the peak hours it can still serve, and returns to the initial battery level by hour 23.

cases.rationale: Reserve is given as an absolute figure and the window 7 PM to 11 PM is hours 19, 20, 21 and 22. Hour 23 is outside the window, so the battery may fall back toward its base minimum there.

cases.label: Single-hour no-discharge window

operator_notes: The battery inverter takes a firmware update from 4 PM to 5 PM, so no discharging is possible during that hour.
IT will migrate the student portal to a new domain in December.

directive_interpretation.explanation: Discharge is blocked for the single hour 16.
This note carries no schedulable constraint for the 24-hour plan.

expected_output.plan_summary: Leaves the battery idle or charging during the firmware hour and concentrates discharge in the surrounding high-tariff hours.

cases.rationale: Tests a one-hour window. 4 PM to 5 PM is start-inclusive and end-exclusive, so the hour list is exactly [16], not [16, 17].

cases.label: Midnight-boundary no-charge window

operator_notes: Do not charge the battery from midnight until 4 AM; the switchgear bay is being rewired.

directive_interpretation.explanation: Charging is blocked for hours 0 through 3 while the bay is rewired.

expected_output.plan_summary: Skips the cheapest overnight charging hours as instructed, charges in the next affordable hours instead, and still restores the initial battery level by the end of hour 23.

cases.rationale: Tests the midnight boundary. Midnight is hour 0 and the window ends exclusive at 4 AM, giving hours 0, 1, 2 and 3, which are among the cheapest charging hours of the day.

cases.label: Late-night grid cap ending at midnight

operator_notes: From 10 PM to midnight, grid import must not exceed 120 kWh in any hour while the substation transformer is derated.

directive_interpretation.explanation: Grid import is capped at 120 kWh per hour for hours 22 and 23.

expected_output.plan_summary: Caps late-night import at 120 kWh by carrying enough stored energy into hour 22, and closes the day at the initial battery level.

cases.rationale: Tests a window that ends at midnight, which is hours 22 and 23 and must not wrap to hour 0. The cap binds against demand, so the battery must be positioned in advance and hour 23 has almost no room to recharge.

cases.label: All notes irrelevant

operator_notes: Please remind the maintenance team that the annual fire drill is scheduled for next month.
The visitor parking lot will be repainted over the weekend.

directive_interpretation.explanation: This note carries no schedulable constraint for the 24-hour plan.
This note carries no schedulable constraint for the 24-hour plan.

expected_output.plan_summary: No operator note changes the schedule, so the plan is the unconstrained cost-optimal one with end-of-day battery neutrality.

cases.rationale: Every note is a distractor. Both entries must be no_op with applies false and a null structured_adjustment, and the schedule must still be optimal under the base constraints.

cases.label: Three active directives of different types

operator_notes: Panel washing runs from noon to 2 PM and usable solar should be treated as about half the forecast.
Hold at least 100 kWh in the battery from 6 PM to 8 PM for the server room.
Discharging is not allowed from 9 AM to 11 AM while the relay coordination test runs.

directive_interpretation.explanation: Usable solar is halved for hours 12 and 13 during panel washing.
Stored energy must stay at or above 100 kWh for hours 18 and 19.
Discharge is blocked for hours 9 and 10 during the relay test.

expected_output.plan_summary: Applies all three directives at once: halved midday solar, a blocked morning discharge window, and a 100 kWh evening floor, while still ending the day at the initial battery level.

cases.rationale: Tests three simultaneous directives of different types in one scenario. All three must appear in note_index order with applies true.

cases.label: Percentage reserve plus overlapping grid cap

operator_notes: Maintain at least 40% of battery capacity from 5 PM to 8 PM for the emergency lighting circuit.
Grid import must stay at or below 170 kWh per hour from 6 PM to 9 PM because the feeder is on a temporary limit.

directive_interpretation.explanation: 40% of the 250 kWh capacity is 100 kWh, required for hours 17, 18 and 19.
Grid import is capped at 170 kWh per hour for hours 18, 19 and 20.

expected_output.plan_summary: Converts the 40% reserve into a 100 kWh floor, respects the 170 kWh feeder cap in the overlapping evening hours, and returns the battery to its starting level.

cases.rationale: Tests a relative reserve combined with a grid cap over partially overlapping windows. Both constraints bind in hours 18 and 19, so the battery must be charged ahead of the evening.

cases.label: Battery fully locked out midday

operator_notes: The battery must not charge from 11 AM to 2 PM during the isolation test.
The battery must also not discharge from 11 AM to 2 PM during that same test.

directive_interpretation.explanation: Charging is blocked for hours 11, 12 and 13.
Discharging is blocked for hours 11, 12 and 13.

expected_output.plan_summary: Keeps the battery idle through the midday isolation test, using solar only as direct demand cover there, and does all cycling outside that window.

cases.rationale: Two notes cover the same hours with different directive types, so the battery is effectively idle for hours 11 to 13. Surplus solar in those hours cannot be stored and is curtailed.

cases.label: Long tight feeder cap requiring pre-charging

operator_notes: From 5 PM until 10 PM, campus grid import must never exceed 140 kWh in any single hour while the incoming feeder is under repair.

directive_interpretation.explanation: Grid import is capped at 140 kWh per hour for hours 17 through 21.

expected_output.plan_summary: Builds the battery up before the evening, holds import at or below 140 kWh for all five restricted hours, and recharges afterwards to end at the initial level.

cases.rationale: Tests a five-hour hard cap well below evening demand. The optimizer must pre-charge earlier in the day to cover roughly 220 kWh of restricted evening demand and still meet end-of-day battery neutrality.
